attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, offered as his estimate.

semantics.note: 'By my estimates' names the basis for a firm present-tense assertion. It is not a probability hedge. The share threshold and the hyperscaler inclusion are kept.

contract.note: Reading the claim as realized revenue in Q2 2025 is an ordinary proxy, but the evaluator chose it. A run-rate reading or a different industry boundary could change the result. The contract flags this.

evidence.note: OpenAI's annualized run rate is company-reported. It is not realized quarterly revenue, and it says nothing about the denominator.
Microsoft's $13B AI run rate is from January 2025, covers a broader AI scope and is annualized. It does not match the period or metric.

Epoch's April 2025 estimate suggests hyperscaler third-party model revenue is large. But it is annualized, not a matched quarter, and lacks a reconciled total, so it does not reliably settle the share.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no matched realized revenue figures for OpenAI, Anthropic and the whole industry, hyperscalers included. The Epoch remark leans against the claim, but it uses a different period and an annualized basis, and reseller double-counting is unresolved. The share cannot be calculated.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: Faithful, and the inflation qualifier and the 'likely much lower' hedge are kept. 'A bargain' is evaluative and cannot be tested. 'A fraction' is the checkable core.

contract.note: The 2006–2015 buildout window and reading 'fraction' as 'materially less' are reasonable plain readings. The window endpoints and the inflation index are supplied by the evaluator.

evidence.note: Gives Amazon-wide cash capex for 2012–2014 only. It has no AWS-specific series and no cumulative total for the buildout.
Gives the 2024 comparator ($77.7B company-wide cash capex) and says 2025 spending is expected to rise. It provides no historical AWS numerator.

reviews.rationale: The comparator side is in the packet, but the cumulative inflation-adjusted cost of the early AWS buildout is not. Only three years of Amazon-wide capex are given, so even an upper bound cannot be built. The 'bargain' part is evaluative.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: An unqualified 'will do it again' is a scoreable forecast with no deadline. The proposition omits 'service availability or functionality' but keeps the core.

contract.note: Requiring both providers is a fair reading of the plural 'these companies'. The 'arbitrarily' test and the requirement that changes be implemented are reasonable.

evidence.note: Anthropic cut off OpenAI's access in August 2025, after the post. This supports recurrence for Anthropic only.
Records Anthropic's terms-of-service justification. This bears on whether the cutoff was arbitrary but does not settle it.
OpenAI announced the Cursor termination in August 2026, effective November 12, 2026, which is after the evaluation date. It was not implemented by the cutoff.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated. The early-resolution rule needs implemented changes by both providers. Only Anthropic's part is shown; OpenAI's Cursor cutoff takes effect after the evaluation date. Not having happened yet does not count as failure.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: In context, 'these companies' points to OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity. The drafter widened it to all generative AI companies. 'Make sense' is partly evaluative.

contract.note: The contract narrows the claim back to the named referents and tests 2024 operating loss. That is an ordinary, fair reading of 'cost too much to run'. The 'make sense' judgment cannot be tested.

evidence.note: OpenAI lost about $5B in 2024, on an unspecified basis. It is not a matched operating-income figure.
An audited S-1, filed before the evaluation date, reports a 2024 operating loss for Anthropic. This supports the Anthropic part only.

reviews.rationale: The support condition needs operating losses at all three companies. Anthropic's is established, OpenAI's loss is on an unclear basis, and there is no readable Perplexity evidence. Nothing contradicts the claim, but the packet does not settle it.
